title: 2-Morita Theory of $E_2$-Algebras and Module Categories
abstract: Building on our previous work on 2-Morita equivalence for $E_2$-algebras using topological pictures, we develop a systematic framework for Morita equivalence of topological orders in different dimensions in terms of $n$-Morita categories $\mathrm{Mrt}_{E_n}(\mathcal{C})$. In this framework, various notions of $n$-Morita equivalence are unified as equivalences of objects in $\mathrm{Mrt}_{E_n}(\mathcal{C})$. We also compare the constructions of higher Morita categories due to Haugseng and to Gwilliam--Scheimbauer.   For $n=1,2$, we prove that the functor $\mathrm{Mod}_n:\mathrm{Mrt}_{E_n}(\mathcal{C})\to \mathrm{Mrt}_{E_{n-1}}(\mathrm{LMod}^{\mathrm{rep}}(\mathcal{C}))$ is an equivalence, relating the algebraic description of higher Morita theory to its realization in terms of module categories. In this formulation, the notion of a bi-bimodule arises naturally and provides a common framework for local and confined modules. Its explicit orientation data, together with the corresponding fusion rules, clarifies the relations among defects arising from condensation in topological orders.
summary: This paper establishes a rigorous mathematical framework, using $n$-Morita categories, to unify the study of higher Morita equivalence for topological orders. By proving the equivalence of the module-realization functor for $n=1, 2$, it provides a powerful tool to relate abstract algebraic structures to concrete module categories describing physical defects.
main_problem: The paper develops a systematic framework to compare and unify different notions of higher Morita equivalence for $E_n$-algebras, particularly in the context of topological orders.
main_result: The module-realization functor $	ext{Mod}_n$ is proven to be an equivalence for $n=1$ and $n=2$, successfully relating the abstract algebraic description to its concrete realization in module categories.
method: The authors utilize advanced category theory, introducing $n$-Morita categories $\mathrm{Mrt}_{E_n}(\mathcal{C})$ and defining the functor $	ext{Mod}_n$ by relating higher algebraic structures (like $E_n$-algebras) to module categories.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to topological orders, which are mathematically described using $E_n$-algebras and their associated module categories, providing a framework for understanding defects and condensation.
key_observables: The structure of higher Morita categories, the explicit orientation data, and the fusion rules governing defects arising from condensation in topological orders.
important_parameters: The dimension $n$ of the topological order ($E_n$-algebras) and the underlying fusion category $\mathcal{C}$.
main_assumptions: The authors do not establish a general equivalence between all three proposed constructions of higher Morita categories (Haugseng, Gwilliam–Scheimbauer, bi-bimodule model) and expect the equivalence to hold for all $n$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates complex bimodule structures involving multiple algebras ($A_1, A_2, A_3, A_4$), while the text describes the structure of the 2-category $	ext{Mrt}E_1(\mathcal{C})$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the $n$-Morita category, comparing different formalisms for higher Morita theory, and culminating in the proof that the module-realization functor $	ext{Mod}_n$ establishes key equivalences for low dimensions ($n=1, 2$).
why_interesting: Topological order theories are deeply connected to condensed matter physics, particularly in describing fractional quantum Hall states and exotic phases of matter, making this highly relevant for understanding strongly correlated systems.
